items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: And they had television orchestras, The Tonight Show Orchestra, and Merv Griffin, and all people like that had bands

ctx.x: That thing about being treated more like an artist rather than just a musician, that’s very true, very very true.

They treated American jazz like a revered product from another land, as we treat European classical music here. And they realized early on that this was the classical music of America. And in most major cities at one time or another they had what you call the “radio bands” now that’s hardly ever been heard of in the United States, the “radio band.” We had television orchestras, The Tonight Show Orchestra, and Merv Griffin, and all people like that had bands, but radio bands? And even some of those radio bands are…
So wonderful that a lot of people were persuaded to move there.
